lessons.title: Parquet
lessons.readme:
# Parquet

[Apache Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/) is a [columnar](https://clickhouse.com/resources/engineering/what-is-columnar-database), binary file format. It's designed for storage efficiency and fast analytics on large datasets.

![Apache Parquet Explainer](/media/storage.googleapis.com/qvault-webapp-dynamic-assets/lesson_videos/Parquet-1920x1080.mp4){captions="captions.vtt"}

## Columnar

"Columnar" means the data is organized by column instead of by row.

Imagine a table like this:

| `product` | `inventory` | `unit_price` |
| --------- | ----------: | -----------: |
| t-shirt   |          10 |        19.99 |
| lamp      |          67 |         9.99 |

A row-based format stores _each record's data_ together. A columnar format instead stores the `product` values together, then the `inventory` values, then the `unit_price` values:

| column       | stored values |
| ------------ | ------------- |
| `product`    | t-shirt, lamp |
| `inventory`  | 10, 67        |
| `unit_price` | 19.99, 9.99   |

This matters because analytics questions often need only a few columns. If you want the average `unit_price`, a columnar format can often avoid reading unrelated columns entirely!

> [!tip]
> Columnar formats are usually better for _analytics_ workloads. Row-based formats are usually better for _transactional_ workloads.

## Binary

Unlike CSV, JSON, or YAML, Parquet is a binary format. Those other formats are _text-based_, meaning you can open them in a text editor and read them.

Parquet files are _not_ human-readable. That's annoying when you want to inspect one manually, but it's great for machines: Parquet stores different data types natively, compresses well, and can be much faster to read and write.

questions.question: SnackStack has a large telemetry archive with many columns, but most analytics queries read only a few columns at a time. Why is Parquet a good fit?
answers: Parquet was on the front page of Hacker News once, so it must be pretty dang good.
Parquet is plain text, so analysts can edit large files by hand.
Parquet is columnar, compressed, typed, and optimized for analytical reads.
Parquet groups together each row's data, which is ideal when reading only a few columns.
questions.answer: Parquet is columnar, compressed, typed, and optimized for analytical reads.

lessons.title: Parquet With Polars
lessons.readme:
# Parquet With Polars

Polars has great Parquet support. Use [`pl.read_parquet()`](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/api/polars.read_parquet.html) to read a Parquet file into a `DataFrame`:

```py
df = pl.read_parquet("sales_data.parquet")
```

You can also use lazy mode with Parquet for _even better_ performance:

```py
df = (
    pl.scan_parquet("large_data.parquet")  # Lazy scan
    .filter(pl.col("year") == 2024)
    .select(["product", "revenue"])
    .collect()
)
```

The [`pl.scan_parquet()`](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/api/polars.scan_parquet.html) function builds a lazy query. Polars can use that query to read only the columns and row groups that it needs.

## Writing Parquet

Polars can write Parquet too:

```py
df.write_parquet("filtered_sales.parquet")
```

Use [`write_parquet()`](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/api/polars.DataFrame.write_parquet.html) when you want to save a processed `DataFrame` back to disk.

Parquet files are usually compressed. Polars supports several compression options, including the modern [`zstd` algorithm](https://github.com/facebook/zstd):

```py
df.write_parquet("filtered_sales.parquet", compression="zstd")
```

> [!info]
> Our browser-based Python environment has limited support for Polars' native Parquet writer, so this lesson's assignment includes a small `write_parquet()` helper for you to call. You won't need it in the real world.

## Assignment

SnackStack's telemetry archive is getting large, so the analytics team wants to build smaller Parquet extracts for focused analysis.

**Complete the `export_device_type_report` function.** It accepts the `source_path` of an input Parquet file; an `output_path` to write results to a new Parquet file; a `device_type`; and a list of `columns`.

1. [ ] [Read](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/api/polars.read_parquet.html) the input Parquet file, passing `source_path` as the file path. **Also pass the argument `use_pyarrow=True`** (this is necessary for our current browser Python environment).
2. [ ] [Keep only rows](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/dataframe/api/polars.DataFrame.filter.html) matching the given `device_type`.
3. [ ] [Select](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/dataframe/api/polars.DataFrame.select.html) only the requested list of `columns`.
4. [ ] Call the provided `write_parquet()` helper, passing the filtered `DataFrame` and `output_path`.
5. [ ] Return the `DataFrame`.

import polars as pl
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq


def export_device_type_report(
    source_path: str, output_path: str, device_type: str, columns: list[str]
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    pass


# Don't touch below this line


def write_parquet(df: pl.DataFrame, output_path: str) -> None:
    table = pa.Table.from_pydict(df.to_dict(as_series=False))
    pq.write_table(table, output_path)

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import polars as pl
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import pytest
from main import export_device_type_report
from polars.testing import assert_frame_equal

TestCase = tuple[pl.DataFrame, str, list[str], pl.DataFrame]


def telemetry(rows: list[tuple[str, str, str, float]]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return pl.DataFrame(
        rows,
        schema=["device_id", "device_type", "region", "temperature_c"],
        orient="row",
    )


run_cases: list[TestCase] = [
    (
        telemetry(
            [
                ("fridge-001", "fridge", "west", 3.7),
                ("oven-002", "oven", "east", 190.0),
                ("fridge-003", "fridge", "north", 4.2),
            ]
        ),
        "fridge",
        ["device_id", "region", "temperature_c"],
        pl.DataFrame(
            [("fridge-001", "west", 3.7), ("fridge-003", "north", 4.2)],
            schema=["device_id", "region", "temperature_c"],
            orient="row",
        ),
    ),
    (
        telemetry(
            [
                ("toaster-004", "toaster", "south", 81.5),
                ("kettle-005", "kettle", "east", 96.3),
                ("toaster-006", "toaster", "west", 77.0),
            ]
        ),
        "toaster",
        ["device_id", "temperature_c"],
        pl.DataFrame(
            [("toaster-004", 81.5), ("toaster-006", 77.0)],
            schema=["device_id", "temperature_c"],
            orient="row",
        ),
    ),
]

submit_cases: list[TestCase] = [
    (
        telemetry(
            [
                ("grill-007", "grill", "south", 210.0),
                ("freezer-008", "freezer", "north", -18.4),
                ("freezer-009", "freezer", "west", -17.8),
                ("microwave-010", "microwave", "east", 42.0),
            ]
        ),
        "freezer",
        ["device_id", "region", "temperature_c"],
        pl.DataFrame(
            [("freezer-008", "north", -18.4), ("freezer-009", "west", -17.8)],
            schema=["device_id", "region", "temperature_c"],
            orient="row",
        ),
    ),
]
submit_cases = [pytest.param(*case, marks=pytest.mark.submit) for case in submit_cases]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_df", "device_type", "cols", "expected"), run_cases + submit_cases
)
def test_export_device_type_report(
    input_df: pl.DataFrame, device_type: str, cols: list[str], expected: pl.DataFrame
) -> None:
    print("\n---------------------------------")
    print("Input DataFrame:")
    print(input_df)
    print(f"\nDevice type to export: {device_type}")
    print(f"Columns to export: {cols}")

    with TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
        source_path = str(Path(temp_dir) / "telemetry.parquet")
        output_path = str(Path(temp_dir) / "report.parquet")
        pq.write_table(
            pa.Table.from_pydict(input_df.to_dict(as_series=False)), source_path
        )

        actual = export_device_type_report(source_path, output_path, device_type, cols)
        actual_written = pl.read_parquet(output_path, use_pyarrow=True)

    print("\nExpected report:")
    print(expected)
    print("\nActual returned report:")
    print(actual)
    print("\nActual written report:")
    print(actual_written)

    assert isinstance(actual, pl.DataFrame)
    assert isinstance(actual_written, pl.DataFrame)
    assert_frame_equal(actual, expected)
    assert_frame_equal(actual_written, expected)
